article: Choosing OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude APIs using current official catalogs and task-specific evaluation
findings: Removed stale 2024/2026 snapshot claims, obsolete model IDs, blanket provider winners, unsupported quality/latency assertions, and old SDK examples; model catalogs and pricing pages now carry volatile details.
Added a reproducible evaluation workflow with matched inputs and settings, task-specific scoring, multiple runs, gradual rollout, and explicit benchmark comparability caveats.

Added latency (TTFT and tail percentiles), per-task cost, retries, caching/batch eligibility, tool authorization, RAG/context tradeoffs, and operational considerations without claiming benchmark results.

Corrected the blanket claim that API data is never retained or used: directs readers to product/tier/feature/contract-specific provider documentation and distinguishes cloud-provider data processing paths.
Preserved original publication date 2026-09-11, added localized lastmod/descriptions, and compared Japanese source with all twelve complete language editions.

meaning.note: Compared the complete edition with the Japanese article: API versus consumer products, official model catalogs, task-specific evaluation, benchmark limitations, latency/cost/operations, provider features, RAG versus context, data handling, security checks, selection process, scope, and update date.

terminology.note: Checked localized terms for API, model catalog and ID, endpoint, evaluation set, benchmark, token/TTFT/p95, prompt caching, batch processing, SDK, tool call, RAG, data processor, retention, and zero data retention.

mathematics.note: The revised article contains no mathematical derivation, formula, or numerical comparison; it avoids unsupported fixed benchmark and price claims.

code.note: The revised article has no source-code examples or executable commands.

links.note: Compared the official OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude model-catalog, pricing, and data-policy links across all editions; all links target provider primary documentation. Link reachability and project-specific terms were not tested here.
